name: Light Columbia Blue
lede: Light Columbia Blue is a pale, slightly grey sky blue, the library's lightened variant of [[columbia-blue]], the shade long tied to Columbia University's athletic color.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The library builds the name in two steps: [[columbia-blue]] as the base entry, "light" catalogued on top as its own variant [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas places the hue at plate XXXIV, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same block (block 181) as light blue, about 3.8 units away in CIEDE2000 [1]. In Munsell notation it sits at 3.2PB 6.8/3.7; measured in LCH it has lightness 69, chroma 13 and hue 260 degrees, near [[periwinkle]] and [[cornflower]] but paler than either [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a match appears in 306 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.3 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 193 [2]. That is ahead of 70 percent of our named colors [2]. It plays a light tone in 41 percent of its appearances [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 22 of 1,674 paintings, 1.3 percent of the 1,674 paintings (22 of them) we have from that century, about 1.3 times the archive's typical rate [2]. Alfred Sisley is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 8 of his 50 archived works, 9.1 times the typical rate [2]. It shares canvases more than chance would predict with [[flax-flower-blue]] [2].

questions.q: Light Columbia Blue is built by adding "light" to which existing color name?
Which painter carries Light Columbia Blue at over 9 times our archive's typical rate?

openers: Alfred Sisley carries Light Columbia Blue at over 9 times our painting archive's typical rate.

issues: Field notes named the wrong painter and lift (claimed Carlos de Haes, 6/29, 17x; real fieldnotes data show Alfred Sisley, 8/50, 9.1x), a wrong painting count, a fabricated 'Norwegian paintings' claim with no supporting country data, and wrong companion colors (periwinkle/sky-blue; the real shared-canvas match is Flax-Flower Blue); corrected to the real counts, painter and companion.
